\section[zögern]{zögern — to hesitate}

\label{lesson:GE-C270-zoegern}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for for years, then the German for for hours.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: zögern}
\textbf{zögern} — \textquotedblleft{}to hesitate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sie zögerte einen Moment und sagte dann Ja.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She hesitated for a moment and then said yes.}
\end{quote}

Regular: \emph{zögerte}, \emph{hat gezögert}. \emph{Ohne zu zögern} — without hesitating.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zögern} is usually traced to Middle High German \emph{zogen} \textquotedblleft{}to pull, to drag\textquotedblright{}, a relative of \emph{ziehen} \textquotedblleft{}to pull\textquotedblright{}: to drag things out. EtymDB lists no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for for years, then the German for for hours, then say \emph{zögern} again

\section[abwarten]{abwarten — to wait and see; to wait for}

\label{lesson:GE-C270-abwarten}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for for hours, then the German for to hesitate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: abwarten}
\textbf{abwarten} — \textquotedblleft{}to wait and see; to wait for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Wir warteten das Ende des Gewitters ab.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We waited for the storm to end.}
\end{quote}

Separable: \emph{wir warten ab}. The saying \emph{Abwarten und Tee trinken} means 'be patient'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{abwarten} is built on \emph{warten} \textquotedblleft{}to wait\textquotedblright{}, from Old High German \emph{wartēn} \textquotedblleft{}to watch, to look after\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), with \emph{ab}: to watch something to its end.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for for hours, then the German for to hesitate, then say \emph{abwarten} again
\end{itemize}

\section[verzögern]{verzögern — to delay; mostly reflexive: sich verzögern, to be delayed}

\label{lesson:GE-C270-verzoegern}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to hesitate, then the German for to wait and see.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: verzögern}
\textbf{verzögern} — \textquotedblleft{}to delay; mostly reflexive: sich verzögern, to be delayed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Flug verzögerte sich um eine Stunde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The flight was delayed by an hour.}
\end{quote}

Often reflexive: \emph{sich verzögern} — to be delayed. \emph{Die Verzögerung} — the delay.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{verzögern} is built on \emph{zögern} \textquotedblleft{}to hesitate\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Middle High German \emph{zogen} \textquotedblleft{}to drag\textquotedblright{}, with the prefix \emph{ver-}; EtymDB lists no parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to hesitate, then the German for to wait and see, then say \emph{verzögern} again

\section[verlaufen]{verlaufen — to go, to proceed; reflexive: to get lost}

\label{lesson:GE-C270-verlaufen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to wait and see, then the German for to delay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: verlaufen}
\textbf{verlaufen} — \textquotedblleft{}to go, to proceed; reflexive: to get lost\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Die Reise verlief ohne Probleme.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The journey went without problems.}
\end{quote}

Perfekt with \emph{sein}: \emph{Alles ist gut verlaufen}. Reflexive, it means to get lost: \emph{Ich habe mich verlaufen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{verlaufen} is inherited from Middle High German \emph{verloufen}, from Old High German \emph{farhloufan} \textquotedblleft{}to pass, to overtake\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{laufen} \textquotedblleft{}to run\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[der Ablauf]{der Ablauf — the sequence of events, the process}

\label{lesson:GE-C270-ablauf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to delay, then the German for to go.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: der Ablauf}
\textbf{der Ablauf} — \textquotedblleft{}the sequence of events, the process\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Der Ablauf des Tages war genau geplant.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The running order of the day was planned exactly.}
\end{quote}

Plural: \emph{die Abläufe}. Also the end of a period: \emph{nach Ablauf der Frist}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{Ablauf} is built on \emph{Lauf} \textquotedblleft{}a run\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{laufen}, Old High German \emph{hloufan} (EtymDB), with \emph{ab}: the way things run off.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the German for to delay, then the German for to go, then say \emph{der Ablauf} again
